text: Hermes Control Center is a cloud-managed, locally executed platform for building and running structured AI workflows.
The platform allows users to create projects, generate agent teams, deploy them to a local runtime, and run real business workflows.
The funding goal for the Hermes Control Center project was $706.
The project's funding was unsuccessful as the goal was not reached by June 6, 2026.
The funding period for the project was from May 7, 2026, to June 6, 2026.
Vincent Wang is the creator of the Hermes Control Center project.
The project is based in Toronto, Canada.
The Hermes Control Center aims to improve the operation of AI tools beyond one-off prompts.
The platform is designed to help teams operate AI tools more effectively than manual methods.
Most AI tools help users chat, but they do not effectively support repeatable business operations.
Teams need a better way to define repeatable workflows, organize AI roles, run tasks on schedule, review outputs, track results, and deliver work consistently.
Hermes Control Center is designed to help teams manage AI projects with a modern web console while execution runs through a local Hermes runtime installed on their own machine.

Hermes Control Center allows users to describe a workflow in plain language, generate an AI agent blueprint, configure supervisors, workers, prompts, tools, and schedules, deploy to a local runtime, monitor runs and tasks, review outputs, and deliver results to their workflow.
Hermes Control Center is built for teams that want AI to do structured work, not just answer questions.
The Hermes Control Center is building an AI-powered outbound research workflow.

The workflow can find potential B2B customers, research their websites, identify relevant contact channels, draft personalized outreach emails, send drafts for human review, and summarize daily results.

The AI-powered outbound research workflow is especially useful for B2B SaaS teams, growth teams, lead generation agencies, marketing agencies, AI automation consultants, consulting firms, and startup operations teams.
To create a project, users start with a simple project description.

Hermes Control Center can generate a structured blueprint that includes a supervisor agent, research agents, contact discovery agents, copywriting agents, reviewer agents, and learning and optimization agents.
Users can deploy the local runtime on macOS, Linux, or Windows WSL2.
Projects can be published from the cloud console to a local node.
The local runtime executes the workflow while the cloud console allows users to track progress.

The Hermes Control Center includes various types of agents such as supervisor agents, research agents, contact discovery agents, copywriting agents, reviewer agents, and learning and optimization agents.
The local runtime can be installed on macOS, Linux, or Windows WSL2.
The local runtime executes workflows while the cloud console allows tracking of various elements such as agents, deployments, nodes, runs, tasks, leads, drafts, approvals, and deliveries.
Outputs from the Hermes Control Center can be reviewed, approved, and delivered through the workflow.
The Hermes Control Center provides more control over how AI runs compared to fully cloud-based systems.
The cloud console offers visibility and control over the AI processes.
The local runtime allows teams to manage execution and provides a clearer separation between configuration and execution.
